cards.explanation: The first challenge is to tell what will happen. The LORD says, “Let them come and tell us what will happen.” (Isaiah 41:22) He wants a prediction, something that can be checked once the day comes. Nobody can fake that one for long, friends.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “Tell the former things, so that we may reflect on them and know the outcome.” (Isaiah 41:22) Then He adds, “Or announce to us what is coming.” So the idols have two ways to answer, the past or the future, and they can't do either.

The answer is that they are gods. The LORD says, “Tell us the things that are to come, so that we may know that you are gods.” (Isaiah 41:23) That's the whole point of the trial, friends. If they can't pass this, the claim doesn't hold.
The word is nothing. The LORD says, “Behold, you are nothing and your work is of no value.” (Isaiah 41:24) Plain and short, friends. I've heard longer rulings on a burnt batch.

The answer is False. The verdict isn't only about the idols. The LORD says, “Anyone who chooses you is detestable.” (Isaiah 41:24) It reaches the ones who pick them, friends, and that's a serious line.

The one He raised up comes from the north and the east. The LORD says, “I have raised up one from the north, and he has come—one from the east who calls on My name.” (Isaiah 41:25) He names both directions, friends. I couldn't tell you why both, because the verse doesn't say.

The answer is True. The LORD says it plainly: “…one from the east who calls on My name.” (Isaiah 41:25) The one He raised up is the one calling on His name, friends. That's the detail the statement is asking about.
Not a single one spoke up ahead of time. The LORD says, “No one announced it, no one foretold it, no one heard your words.” (Isaiah 41:26) Zero for the whole lineup, friends, and that was the test.
The LORD gave Jerusalem a herald of good news. He says, “…I gave to Jerusalem a herald of good news.” (Isaiah 41:27) A herald is someone who brings word, friends, and here the word is good news.
The answer is True. The LORD says, “when I ask them, they have nothing to say.” (Isaiah 41:28) He asks, and the idols give Him silence. I've had a quiet oven act more helpful than that, friends.

The word is delusion. The LORD says, “See, they are all a delusion; their works amount to nothing; their images are as empty as the wind.” (Isaiah 41:29) He calls the idols a delusion, friends, and He says their images are as empty as the wind.
